name: test-page
description: Parity testing in <15 min: plan (gate) -> author tests in parallel (one agent per module, 6 slots) -> run all modules in parallel (mutating ones serialized) -> one fix round over all modules (max 2) -> deterministic final report (gate). Chat shows every phase as tables (CHAT-RENDER). Open the repo folder as the workspace.

steps.prompt:
Page: {{page}}. Page dir: .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/ (all paths are relative to the repo root, which is the workspace). Phase 0 (Plan). This step owns gate 1 (plan sign-off).
Rules: shell ONLY `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action ...` (no dotnet, no inline scripts, no sleep/poll loops, Test-NetConnection, Get-Content or git). Read state with file tools only; lifecycle.ps1 is the only writer of status.json, timings.json, PROGRESS.md and chat/. Human text never goes on a command line: write it to .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/gate-response.txt with a file tool and pass -ResponseFile. -Message values are single-quoted, embedded ' doubled, one line of at most 200 chars, no $ and no backtick. Never edit .kiro/test-project/Harness/**, .kiro/test-project/Reports/** or the Reference source (status.json paths.reference, appsettings ReferenceSourcePath). No confirmation questions outside the designed gates. Auto-fix selector/timing/build errors up to 3 times, then record the evidence and continue. Chat renders: at each render milestone below run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action render -Page {{page}} -View <view>` and send ONE send_message: first every `CHAT-RENDER <absolute path>` line printed by render, exactly and in the printed order (one per view and each report section is one table; only the plan prints an overview then one per module), then the summary line printed by render, then (gates only) the question; severity info, or warning at a gate. If render exits 1, run it once more; if it fails again, send the message without a CHAT-RENDER line, quoting the [render] FAIL line, and continue. No info messages other than CHAT-RENDER relays. Shell timeouts: pass at least 150000 ms for every wait call and at least 600000 ms for run-page without -Detach, rerun-target and report.

1. Run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action progress -Page {{page}} -Phase 0 -Message 'Plan step started'`.
2. Read .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/status.json and .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/state-map/plan.json with file tools (either may be missing).
3. RESUME: if plan.json exists AND status.json plan.signedOff == true AND status.json plan.signedOffRevision == plan.json revision, do not re-plan. Run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action gate -Page {{page}} -Gate plan_signoff -State pending`, then render -View plan, then send ONE send_message warning (every CHAT-RENDER line printed by render in order, then the summary, then 'Plan revision <n> signed off at <plan.signedOffAt>. Reply confirm to resume with it, or describe changes.'). Then end your turn: the step stays paused until the human replies. Never send success before `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action gate -Page {{page}} -Gate plan_signoff -State confirmed` exits 0. When the reply arrives, go to step 6.
4. OTHERWISE run Phase 0 (#phase-0-analysis.md, #state-machine-testing.md, and #pagination-sorting-standards.md for grid pages), starting from the existing plan.json if present: read the reference and target page source; define ALL states with key indicators; design modules as complete end-to-end user workflows with numbered steps (group by user goal, never by action type); prefer at most 6 modules (more is allowed, but author slot 6 then writes modules 6..N one after another and authoring slows down); per step the CHANGES and STAYS SAME fields (fields only, never values) plus checksText: one plain-English sentence per check describing the expected behaviour without any data value, because nothing has run yet (e.g. 'The pager range text (View x - y of z) advances to the next page's numbers.', 'The total count stays the same.', 'Save stays disabled.'); expected values come from the Reference run; the CSS capture plan per state including transient elements. Write state-map/states.md, transitions.md, assertions.md, css-capture-plan.md, plan.json = {page, revision, states:[{id, name, howReached, indicators:[...]}], modules:[{id, name, userStory, dataEffect, plannedSteps, referenceTest 'Reference{{page}}_Mod<X>', targetTest '{{page}}_Mod<X>', cssStates:[...], steps:[{id, action, changes:[fields], staysSame:[fields], checks:[...], checksText:[sentences]}], notTested:[{item, reason}]}], fieldLabels:{<field pattern>: <plain-English label>}} where fieldLabels names every field the tests will assert, with {n}/{name} placeholders (e.g. 'row[{n}].name.text': 'Payor Name in row ID {n}', 'saveButton.enabled': 'Save button', 'pager.info': 'Pager text', 'grid.rowCount': 'Rows shown') with steps.length == plannedSteps, and css-map.json = {elements:[{name, state, reference <selector>, target <selector that does not depend on classes a fix would add>, properties {<css property>: HIGH|MEDIUM|LOW}, accepted {<property>: <reason>} optional, role grid|row|header|pager|filter optional}]} with elements for every state listed in any cssStates; for every planned state that shows a grid add geometry-only elements (properties {}) with role row (matches every data row), grid (grid container without the pager), header (header row) and pager, plus role filter (filter panel) on the first state that shows it, element names unique per state and no pre-accepted layout.* metrics (the generator compares layout.height, layout.rowHeight, layout.headerHeight, layout.gapToPager, layout.gapToGrid). dataEffect rule: a module with any Save/persist step is 'mutating'; Cancel-only, filter, sort or paging modules are 'read-only' unless something persists (the runner serializes mutating modules and restarts the service after them). Revision rule: a new plan starts at revision 1; bump revision by 1 ONLY when some module's id, plannedSteps, referenceTest, targetTest, cssStates or steps[].id list change or a module is added or removed; wording-only edits to state-map/*.md, notTested or name, and adding userStory, dataEffect, states, checksText or fieldLabels, do not bump it. The runner enforces the rule: gate plan_signoff fingerprints exactly these fields and, when they changed while plan.json kept the recorded revision, rewrites plan.json revision to the recorded revision + 1 itself. Still bump per the rule, and re-read plan.json after every gate call: its revision is the final one.
5. GATE: run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action gate -Page {{page}} -Gate plan_signoff -State pending`, then `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action render -Page {{page}} -View plan`, then send ONE send_message warning: every CHAT-RENDER line printed by render (in order), then the summary, line 3 'Reply confirm to sign off, or describe changes.' Then end your turn: the step stays paused until the human replies. Never send success before `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action gate -Page {{page}} -Gate plan_signoff -State confirmed` exits 0.
6. REPLY: if the whole reply (trimmed, case-insensitive) is confirm, approve, yes or ok: write the reply verbatim to .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/gate-response.txt with a file tool, run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action gate -Page {{page}} -Gate plan_signoff -State confirmed -ResponseFile .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/gate-response.txt`, then finish with send_message success 'Plan revision <n> signed off (<module ids>). Next: authoring in parallel.' Any other reply is revision feedback: FIRST run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action progress -Page {{page}} -Phase 0 -Message 'Revising plan (feedback received)'`, then update the plan files (bump revision only per the rule), then repeat step 5. If a gate command exits 1, fix the plan file and retry (at most 3 times), then send_message error with the console line.

1. Read .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/status.json and .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/state-map/plan.json with file tools. If status.json plan.signedOff != true, or status.json plan.signedOffRevision != plan.json revision: send_message warning 'waiting for plan sign-off (status.json plan.signedOff is false)', write nothing, and end your turn. This pauses the slot; never end it with success or error for this reason. When you are resumed, start again at step 1.
2. If plan.json modules has fewer than 1 entries, send_message success 'slot 1 unused' immediately, with no shell call.
3. Your module list: slots 1-5 handle only plan.json modules[k-1]; slot 6 handles modules[5] and every later module, one after another. For this slot that is modules[0]. Never touch another module's files. No progress calls in this step (no page lock contention).
4. For each module X in your list: read state-map/transitions.md, assertions.md, css-capture-plan.md and the plan.json entry of X (steps[] with id/action/changes/staysSame/checks, cssStates, dataEffect, and the top-level states[]). Write ONLY .kiro/test-project/Modules/{{page}}.Mod<X>/Reference{{page}}Module<X>_v2.cs (test method = plan.json referenceTest) and .kiro/test-project/Modules/{{page}}.Mod<X>/{{page}}Module<X>_v2.cs (test method = plan.json targetTest), following #module-test-standards.md and the existing .kiro/test-project/Modules/*/*_v2.cs pattern (ModuleTestRunner, ExecuteStep with the plan step ids, AssertEquals / AssertChanged / AssertUnchanged / Assert, Capture(stateId, field, value), CssCompareHelper.DiscoverAndCaptureAll at every planned CSS state, GenerateReport). Skip writing only when both files exist, both line-1 header revisions equal status.json plan.fingerprintRevision (== plan.json revision; the runner bumps it when the plan structure changed) and both headers' steps=<k> equal the module's plannedSteps.
5. Resume: line 1 of every test file is '// plan-revision: <n>; steps=<k>' (<k> = the module's plannedSteps). A test file that already exists, has a header revision equal to status.json plan.fingerprintRevision (== plan.json revision) and steps= equal to plannedSteps, and builds is left untouched. A file whose header revision differs from plan.fingerprintRevision, or whose steps= differs from plannedSteps, must be updated even if it builds. Update = edit only the steps whose plan entry changed, then set the header to the new revision; never regenerate an existing file wholesale. A Reference test file whose module is unchanged (same id, plannedSteps, test names and cssStates as in status.json) is never edited; only its header is bumped. New files get the header on line 1.
6. Authoring invariants: Target step names are identical to the Reference step names. Every Reference assertion is mirrored on Target with the same (step, field, type) and in the same order. Every Reference Capture(state, field) is mirrored on Target in the same step, with the same state and field; the value is the Target runtime value. Only EQUALS/CONTAINS expected constants are copied verbatim from the Reference assertion with the same (step, field, type); CHANGES and STAYS SAME are mirrored as assertions whose before-value comes from Target runtime state (a value the Target test read earlier), never as a copied constant; BOOL has no constant to copy. assertions.md chooses fields, never values. Never weaken an assertion.
7. Build: run `.\.kiro\test-project\lifecycle.ps1 -Action build-module -Page {{page}} -Module <X>` until exit 0, with at most 3 fix attempts per distinct error (log: .kiro/app-testing/{{page}}/logs/build-<X>.log). An exit 0 that prints '[build-module] WARN ... not authored yet' or 'Tgt not authored' means a test file is missing: write it and build again. A step count in the [build-module] line that differs from plannedSteps is not an error.
8. End with ONE send_message success, one line per handled module: 'Module X: Ref 13 steps/54 assertion calls, Tgt 13/38, build PASS (rev 1)' (numbers from the [build-module] PASS line), or 'Module X: unchanged (rev 1), build PASS', or after 3 failed attempts 'Module X: build FAIL: <first error CS line>'. A build FAIL still ends in success, so the other modules and the run continue; run-page reports that module as NOT_RUN.

(2) test-expectation: set the Target EQUALS/CONTAINS expected constant to the Reference EQUALS/CONTAINS constant with the same (step, field, type), copied verbatim; that is the only allowed constant change; CHANGES and STAYS SAME are never edited under this rule. (3) test-coverage, plus the missingAssertions and missingCaptures of ANY finding: add a missing step to the Target test mirroring the Reference step; add a missing assertion to the existing Target step at the Reference position; add a missing runner.Capture(state, field, <Target value>) in the same Target step at the same position as in the Reference test body (including the NAV/PRE steps), where <Target value> is what the Target test reads at that point; EQUALS/CONTAINS constants copied verbatim, CHANGES/STAYS SAME take their before-value from Target runtime state; adding never loosens or removes existing assertions; on an app or test-selector finding add its missing assertions and captures in the same round. A theme group (same role class, property and Reference/Target values on many elements, e.g. 'Buttons: border-radius 4px -> 3px, 46 elements') is fixed with ONE CSS rule or theme token change in the Target source (TargetSourcePath), never per element; individual groups (missing/extra elements, layout.*, responsive.*, geometry) follow their Action per element. findingIds = ['css:group:<key>'] (key from css_groups.json).
